messages:
jen-support: FYI incoming ticket #34567 — customer says they get repeatedly kicked to MFA and logged out right after accepting device trust. Happens when they switch from office wifi -> mobile data. Started around 08:30 UTC this morning. They provided a short repro.
alex-g: can you paste the customer repro steps and any request IDs? also which browser / webview?
jen-support: customer says Android webview (in-app browser). Repro steps they gave:
1) SSO login -> approve device trust
2) land on app, everything okay
3) toggle network (wifi -> cellular)
4) try an operation that hits /v1/query -> gets a 401 + prompted to re-auth
They attached a curl they ran from a proxy that reproduces it. Repro curl:
```
curl -v -H "Cookie: session=eyJhbGci..." https://api.redwood.inference/v1/query
```
Response from API:
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
content-type: application/json
{"error":"invalid_session","message":"session cookie missing or expired","request_id":"req_0x9a7b"}
```
jen-support: they also captured the Set-Cookie on login. It looks like: `Set-Cookie: session=eyJ...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=2592000` — they think SameSite might be dropping the cookie when the webview does a cross-site navigation during the network change.
raj-p: repro steps make sense. mobile webviews + network changes can cause the browser to re-evaluate cookie policies. SameSite=Lax blocks some cross-site POSTs but should allow top-level GET navigations. But in webview context it can be weird. +1 to verifying cookie header on the failing request. can you get the raw request headers for req_0x9a7b?
samira-ops: digging into session-service logs for that request id now. quick note: we rolled session-service at 07:58 UTC (release/session-service@2026.09.01.07). deploy-bot: "deploy finished: session-service release/session-service@2026.09.01.07 (commit f2a9c3d) — started 07:50 UTC, finished 07:58 UTC".
alex-g: ok if the deploy is in the window we need to treat as potential regression. samira can you check recent changes? especially anything touching cookie attributes or rotation logic.
samira-ops: scanning commits... there was a change to cookie rotation to harden CSRF flows. It defaults SameSite to Lax but we added a tenant-configurable override. I see a config flag: `SESSION_SAMESITE_OVERRIDE` - default null, but staging/production deploy sets it to Lax now. The change also added a short-lived intermediate cookie during rotation; maybe webview drops that one on network change.
mfa-bot: MFA trust token issued for user u_1023, device-trust TTL=86400s, trust_cookie=trst_8a7c (expires in 86400s)
jen-support: customer confirms they see trst cookie set, but on failing request the trst cookie is not sent. They can reproduce on their device consistently by toggling wifi off.
raj-p: collect packet / header dump pls. If cookie isn't sent, it's either SameSite semantics, domain mismatch, or the webview destroyed session store during network change. Also check whether the webview does a redirect to an auth domain that changes site-context; that would cause Lax to drop cookie on POST/navigations.
alex-g: quick mitigation we can do for this customer: set SameSite=None for session & trust cookies for that tenant (we can flip SESSION_SAMESITE_OVERRIDE to None) and reissue session cookie. That should allow the cookie to be sent in cross-site contexts. But we need to validate security impact.
samira-ops: agreed. I can patch config for tenant: acme-corp (their tenant) and restart only the session-service on that shard. Will do a canary: update config, restart one instance.
deploy-bot: "rolling restart: session-service shard-12 (canary)"
samira-ops: canary restart done. I issued a test on an internal android webview and toggled network — cookie persisted and request succeeded (200). Request id: req_0x9a8c. Logs:
```
[session-service] request=req_0x9a8c cookie=session=eyJ... action=accepted
[session-service] trace=rotation_skipped for active session
```
alex-g: good. jen-support, can you ask the customer to test while I coordinate broader rollout? also gather the original failing request ids and any screenshots they have of devtools (if possible on webview).
jen-support: pinged customer with canary details and asked for a retry. they replied "works now" for the one user. they still have a few devices failing — asked to try clearing app cache and update webview component. they also provided one request id from a failing device: req_0x9b0d.
raj-p: will pick up deeper root cause. next steps: 1) collect failing request ids (req_0x9a7b, req_0x9b0d) 2) compare headers and cookie send behavior vs successful canary req_0x9a8c 3) add additional telemetry around cookie attribute evaluation to session-service 4) decide whether to roll SameSite=None for all tenants or introduce smarter logic (e.g., SameSite=None for mobile webviews / legacy in-app browsers)
nick-product: product concern — broad rollout of SameSite=None increases CS risk for some flows. we need a security review before global change. fine to apply tenant-level override as a supported mitigation.
jen-support: customer updated that clearing app cache + webview update fixed 2 of 3 failing devices; one remaining device still fails even after cache clear. they've accepted temporary tenant fix while we investigate.
alex-g: great. raj, scope: please triage root cause and get a postmortem if we decide to keep tenant override long-term. assign ownership to eng-runtime? seems related to cookie rotation and in-app browser edge cases.
raj-p: assigning to eng-runtime. I'll start a deeper trace run and surface config diff. ETA initial findings 24h.
jen-support: I'll update customer and keep ticket open. action items: @raj-p owns root cause, @samira-ops did canary + tenant patch, @alex-g will coordinate rollback/rollout and customer comms. closing loop here. :thumbsup:
